new.title: Tour the Palais des Papes, the Gothic papal fortress
new.desc: The largest Gothic palace in Europe combines the austere Palais Vieux of Benedict XII with the lavish Palais Neuf of Clement VI, built in the 14th century when the popes lived in Avignon. It served as a barracks after the Revolution and became a national museum in 1906. It is part of the UNESCO-listed historic centre.
new.tip: Book a timed ticket online in summer to skip the queue, and allow two hours. The Cour d'honneur is the main stage of the Festival d'Avignon in July.
new.q: Palais des Papes, Place du Palais, Avignon

new.title: Walk onto the Pont Saint-Bénezet, the Pont d'Avignon
new.desc: The medieval bridge over the Rhône was first built between 1177 and 1185, and floods repeatedly destroyed arches until only four remained. Its legend ties it to the shepherd Bénezet, and the nursery song made it famous worldwide. It became a UNESCO site in 1995.
new.tip: The best photos of the bridge are from the Rocher des Doms or the Barthelasse bank at sunset. Entry is ticketed and includes an audioguide.
new.q: Pont Saint-Bénezet, Rue Ferruce, Avignon

new.title: Stroll the Rocher des Doms garden for the Rhône view
new.desc: This hilltop park sits on a limestone spur above the Rhône beside the Palais des Papes and is considered the cradle of Avignon. The English-style garden has lawns, basins and shaded paths with views over the river and the Barthelasse. It was being renovated from October 2024 with parts reopening in stages.
new.tip: Entry is free. Come at the end of the day for the best light on the bridge and the Mont Ventoux horizon.
new.q: Jardin du Rocher des Doms, Avignon

new.title: See Italian primitives at the Musée du Petit Palais
new.desc: The former archbishops' palace on the square of the Palais des Papes holds over 300 Italian primitives, including the Campana collection, plus Avignon School paintings. The building was rebuilt in the late 15th century by Archbishop Julien de la Rovère, the future Pope Julius II. It also shows 14th-century funerary sculpture.
new.tip: The tourism office lists a closure from 16 to 30 November, so check before going in late autumn. Hours are afternoons on weekdays and all day at weekends.
new.q: Musée du Petit Palais, Place du Palais, Avignon

new.title: Discover contemporary art at the Collection Lambert
new.desc: Yvon Lambert's collection fills two 18th-century mansions, the Hôtels de Caumont and Montfaucon, built by Jean-Baptiste Franque. The donation to the French state became official in July 2012. A rotating selection of the collection is shown at the Hôtel de Caumont, with temporary shows next door.
new.tip: Closed on Mondays in most seasons; confirm hours on the museum site. The entrance is on rue Violette.
new.q: Collection Lambert, 5 Rue Violette, Avignon

new.title: Browse paintings at the Musée Calvet
new.desc: Avignon's main fine arts museum occupies an 18th-century mansion at 65 rue Joseph Vernet and shows paintings from the 16th to the 20th century with a focus on classicism and romanticism. The archaeological collections are in the Musée Lapidaire, in the former Jesuit chapel, as part of the same museum.
new.tip: Winter hours run from 1 November to 31 March, so check the website. The courtyard garden is worth a stop.
new.q: Musée Calvet, 65 Rue Joseph Vernet, Avignon

new.title: Visit Notre-Dame des Doms cathedral and the tomb of John XXII
new.desc: Avignon's cathedral beside the Palais des Papes is a Provençal Romanesque church from about 1150, enlarged with chapels in the 14th and 17th centuries. A gilded Virgin crowns the bell tower. Inside, the Gothic tomb of Pope John XXII is regarded as its most important artwork.
new.tip: Entry is free. Combine it with the Rocher des Doms right behind it.
new.q: Cathédrale Notre-Dame des Doms, Place du Palais, Avignon

new.title: Follow the papal ramparts around Avignon
new.desc: The stone walls of more than 4 km around the old town took their present form under the popes in the 14th century, and Avignon is one of the few French cities to keep its full circuit. The gates were pierced through the walls over time. The walls were classed as historic monuments from the 19th century.
new.tip: Walking the outside of the wall takes about an hour. Porte de la République and Porte Saint-Lazare are good start points.
new.q: Porte de la République, Remparts d'Avignon, Avignon

new.title: Find Van Gogh and Doucet's taste at the Musée Angladon
new.desc: This small museum in an 18th-century mansion shows the collection of the couturier Jacques Doucet, passed down to Jean Angladon and Paulette Martin. It opened on 15 November 1996 and draws around 25,000 visitors a year. The Fondation Angladon-Dubrujeaud runs it.
new.tip: Open afternoons, with full admission around 8 euros. Last entry is 17:15.
new.q: Musée Angladon, 5 Rue Laboureur, Avignon

new.title: Sit on Place de l'Horloge beside the town hall and carousel
new.desc: The main square of the old town is lined with café terraces and faces the 19th-century Hôtel de Ville, whose medieval-style clock tower has mechanical figures that strike the hours. The Opéra and a Belle Époque carousel stand on the same square.
new.tip: Busy in July during the festival; at the start of the morning it is calm. The carousel runs all year.
new.q: Place de l'Horloge, Avignon

new.title: Wander the rue des Teinturiers and its water wheels
new.desc: A canal of the Sorgue runs along this shaded street, where mills once drove up to 23 wheels in 1817 for printed cotton (indiennes), silk and tanneries until 1894. A few wheels survive, some restored. The street has been a protected site since 1932.
new.tip: The street is lively with café terraces and during the festival. Quieter on weekday mornings.
new.q: Rue des Teinturiers, Avignon

new.title: Step into the Musée Louis Vouland decorative arts
new.desc: A 17th and 18th-century mansion at 17 rue Victor Hugo houses the decorative arts collection of the industrialist Louis Vouland, who left it to the Fondation de France after his death in 1973. It shows Provençal and Languedoc arts and temporary exhibitions, and has a garden.
new.tip: Open afternoons, closed Mondays per an earlier listing; check vouland.com. It is not accessible to reduced mobility visitors.
new.q: Musée Louis Vouland, 17 Rue Victor Hugo, Avignon

new.title: Dine on Pérouvence cuisine at Hiély-Lucullus
new.desc: Open since 1938 in a Majorelle-style room, this restaurant is described as the oldest gastronomic table in Avignon. Gérald and Patricia Azoulay cook Pérouvence, a blend of Provençal and Peruvian influences. Gault&Millau rates it 14.5/20.
new.tip: A menu of the day is cheaper than the tasting menu. Opening days vary by source, so phone ahead.
new.q: Hiély-Lucullus, 5 Rue de la République, Avignon

new.title: Book a table at Maison Christian Etienne, now Sevin
new.desc: The restaurant at 10 rue de Mons stands at the foot of the Palais des Papes, with a terrace facing the walls. It was led for decades by Chef Christian Etienne, who held a Michelin star from 1988, and is now listed as Restaurant Sevin.
new.tip: Closed Wednesday and Thursday per the 2025 listing. Reserve the terrace for lunch.
new.q: Restaurant Sevin, 10 Rue de Mons, Avignon

new.title: Eat a terroir menu at La Mirande, facing the Palais
new.desc: The restaurant of the Hôtel La Mirande on place de l'Amirande serves a gastronomic menu built on local seasonal produce. Gault&Millau gives it 15/20 and Michelin lists a star; the chef has changed recently. The hotel also runs a bistro room, La Salle à Manger.
new.tip: Ask about the current chef and menu when booking. La Salle à Manger is the lighter and cheaper option.
new.q: La Mirande, 4 Place de l'Amirande, Avignon

new.title: Have a regional lunch at La Fourchette on rue Racine
new.desc: A small traditional French restaurant at 17 rue Racine inside the walls, serving fresh produce and mostly regional wines. Michelin lists it at the two-euro-sign level and Gault&Millau at 12/20 with a price near 43 euros.
new.tip: Opening days differ between listings, so reserve and confirm.
new.q: La Fourchette, 17 Rue Racine, Avignon

new.title: Take tea and scones at Simple Simon
new.desc: A long-running British-style tea room and restaurant at 26 rue de la Petite Fusterie, known for brunch, scones, cheesecake and a good choice of teas. Gault&Millau lists it.
new.tip: Reservations are advised and cash may be preferred; hours vary by source.
new.q: Simple Simon, 26 Rue de la Petite Fusterie, Avignon

new.title: Pick up bread and pastry at La Fabrique des Saveurs
new.desc: A bakery-pastry shop on rue Grivolas run by pastry chef Nicolas Martinez and baker Arnaud Bertrand. Gault&Millau describes quality bread, viennoiserie and a terrace.
new.tip: Come in the morning for viennoiseries and bread, and sit on the terrace.
new.q: La Fabrique des Saveurs, Rue Grivolas, Avignon

new.title: Shop Provençal delicacies at Maison Brémond 1830
new.desc: The Avignon delicatessen at 34 rue de la Grande Fusterie belongs to the brand founded in 1830 in Aix-en-Provence and sells Provençal sweets and food gifts.
new.tip: Listed hours show 9:00 to 19:30 at weekends; check the website for weekdays. Papalines are more reliably found at Recolin.
new.q: Maison Brémond 1830, 34 Rue de la Grande Fusterie, Avignon

new.title: Have a terrace meal at the Brasserie de l'Horloge
new.desc: A brasserie at 26 place de l'Horloge with a terrace on the central square facing the Hôtel de Ville and the Opéra.
new.tip: Prices on the square are higher in July; book ahead during the festival.
new.q: Brasserie de l'Horloge, 26 Place de l'Horloge, Avignon

new.title: Sit at Le Grand Café on the Escaliers Sainte-Anne
new.desc: Le Grand Café operates from La Manutention at 4 rue des Escaliers Sainte-Anne with about 70 outdoor tables, close to the Palais des Papes.
new.tip: A good spot for a drink after the palace visit. Check opening hours in winter.
new.q: Le Grand Café La Manutention, 4 Rue des Escaliers Sainte-Anne, Avignon

new.title: Taste Côtes du Rhône at Au Cœur des Vins on rue Galante
new.desc: A wine bar and caviste at 11 rue Galante near the Place de l'Horloge with on-site tasting. It is listed by Gault&Millau among artisans.
new.tip: Ask for a Côtes du Rhône or Ventoux by the glass. Confirm opening hours before going.
new.q: Au Cœur des Vins, 11 Rue Galante, Avignon

new.title: Catch a play at the Festival d'Avignon in July
new.desc: The 80th Festival d'Avignon ran from 4 to 25 July 2026, with 47 creations in 40 venues and 136,000 seats from 7 euros. The Cour d'honneur of the Palais des Papes is its main stage.
new.tip: Tickets go on sale in the spring and the popular shows sell out. The next edition is in July 2027.
new.q: Cour d'honneur du Palais des Papes, Avignon

new.title: Join the Festival Off parade and shows in July
new.desc: The Festival Off ran for its 60th edition from 4 to 25 July 2026 in step with the In, with the opening Grande Parade at Place Pie on 3 July and the Village du Off as its hub. Listings count over 1,600 shows across more than 130 venues.
new.tip: Pick shows from the programme and expect flyers in every street. Dates move slightly each year.
new.q: Place Pie, Avignon

new.title: Cycle the Île de la Barthelasse loop
new.desc: France Vélo Tourisme loop no. 4 circles the largest river island in Europe, with about 700 hectares of orchards, in 13 to 14 km on easy shared lanes. It offers views of the Palais des Papes and herons.
new.tip: A free river shuttle crosses from quai de la Ligne near the bridge, and Velopop bikes can be rented. Mistral wind can be strong.
new.q: Île de la Barthelasse, Avignon

new.title: Cruise the Rhône on the Mireio past the bridge
new.desc: The Compagnie des Grands Bateaux de Provence runs the restaurant boat Mireio from Allée de l'Oulle, with cruises past the Pont Saint-Bénezet and the Palais des Papes. Some trips reach Arles through the Vallabrègues lock, including Sunday lunch cruises in 2026.
new.tip: Book on the company site; the short cruise costs about 13 euros per a 2023 article. Check current schedules.
new.q: Mireio, Grands Bateaux de Provence, Allées de l'Oulle, Avignon

new.title: Browse the Sunday flea market on Place des Carmes
new.desc: A weekly flea market is held on Place des Carmes every Sunday from 8:00 to 13:00, and the centre-ville food market runs on Saturday mornings in the same area. Entry is free.
new.tip: Go early for the best finds. Check avignon.fr for the schedule.
new.q: Place des Carmes, Avignon

new.title: Browse the stalls of Les Halles, Tuesday to Sunday
new.desc: The covered market on Place Pie has about 40 to 50 traders selling Provençal produce, cheese, wine and fish. The 1899 hall celebrated 125 years in 2024, and a vegetable wall by Patrick Blanc covers its outside.
new.tip: Open mornings until 14:00, closed Mondays. Saturdays at 11:00 a chef cooking demo is reported.
new.q: Les Halles d'Avignon, Place Pie, Avignon

new.title: Cook with a chef at Cuisine Centr'Halles
new.desc: Cuisine Centr'Halles at 18 place Pie offers cooking classes and lunches inside the covered market using products bought from the stalls.
new.tip: Closed Mondays. Book the workshop ahead.
new.q: Cuisine Centr'Halles, 18 Place Pie, Avignon

new.title: Sample 24 wines at Le Vin Devant Soi
new.desc: A caviste in the historic centre with Enomatic fountains offering 24 wines for tasting at any time, with Côtes du Rhône a major part of the range.
new.tip: Listings give two addresses, 1 rue Saint-Agricol and rue du Collège du Roure, so check on the way.
new.q: Le Vin Devant Soi, 1 Rue Saint-Agricol, Avignon
